# Draft:World Orelha Awareness Day

}}
Legacy and Commemoration. Since the events of January 2026, the memory of Orelha has transitioned from a local tragedy to a symbol for international animal rights. Orelha World Day (January 4)A global movement, spearheaded by animal welfare advocates and the production company Andares Productions, has proposed designating January 4th as "Orelha World Day" (or World Day for Stray and Abused Animals). The date marks the anniversary of the attack on Orelha and serves as a day of awareness for the "invisible" stray populations worldwide. The proposal aims to promote "Radical Kindness" by encouraging communities to provide food, shelter, and medical care to local community animals. Legislative Advocacy: Using the day to lobby for stricter animal cruelty laws, similar to the proposed "Lei Orelha" in Brazil.Public Education: Raising awareness about the estimated 70 million stray animals in the U.S. and millions more globally. Global Petition: A Change.org petition to officially recognize the day has garnered significant international support. As of April 2026, the petition has collected over 170,000 signatures, calling on the United States government and international bodies to formally add the date to the calendar of environmental and animal welfare observances. Documentary: I Am Orelha, I Matter. The case and the subsequent movement are the subject of an upcoming documentary titled I Am Orelha, I Matter (Eu Sou Orelha, Eu Importo). The film explores the "community dog" model, the judicial proceedings in Florianópolis, and the rise of the #JustiçaPorOrelha movement. In April 2026, promotional materials for the film went viral, further amplifying the call for the January 4th designation.
References
Following the 2026 events, a movement emerged to designate January 4th as Orelha's World Day to advocate for community animals. An associated global petition reached a milestone of 170,000 signatures by April 2026.
